title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from pp.12-14. L is a finite ground set and P(L) its power set. Admissible 'figures' are elements A of P(L) carrying an interior A° and a boundary ∂A. M is the poset of 'multifigures/multiplicités' X ⊂ P(L), with ∅ ∉ X (p.12 notes that A admissible implies A° ≠ ∅, hence A ≠ ∅). By p.12 the minimal elements of M are the singletons {A}. Any X with a minimal element A lies above {A}. Every {A} with A ≠ L lies in the same connected component as the {{x}}, x ∈ L. The link uses an upper bound built from A, {x} and A ∪ {x}.

This page finishes the argument in three steps.
(1) The exceptional element {L} is also in that component. This is shown with the multiplicity {{{x}},{L∖{x}}} (as transcribed), which links {L} to the {{x}}.
(2) Degenerate cases. If L = ∅, M = ∅ and Grothendieck calls it connected. If card L = 1, P(L) = {∅, L}, and the subsets Q with ∅ ∉ Q are ∅ and {L}. So M = {{L}} is a single point, hence (0-)connected.
(3) Proposition. If card L ≤ 1, M is connected. If card L ≥ 1 (should read ≥ 2), all X ∈ M having a minimal element lie in one connected component. Hence, restricting to finite figures/multiplicities, which Grothendieck says is enough for his purposes, M is connected.

Consequence: his axiom C4 is satisfied trivially in this model. That axiom asks for M to decompose into connected components, with elements of different components incomparable, and here the decomposition is 'automatic'. The purpose is to check that this concrete combinatorial model satisfies the axioms (C1-C4…) of his abstract 'algebra of figures'. The next page then builds the join F⊠G = {A ∪ B}, with ∂(A∪B) = ∂A∪B ∪ A∪∂B, to show further properties, e.g. that disjoint multifigures have a common upper bound.
errors: The second case of the Proposition says 'card L ≥ 1'. Since card L = 1 was just treated separately, it should be 'card L ≥ 2', or the case should be stated as 'L ≠ ∅' with a different argument.
Calling the empty poset (L = ∅) 'connexe' breaks the standard convention that the empty space or category is not connected. It is a harmless convention here but technically sloppy.
The parenthetical as transcribed says elements of different components are 'comparables'. It must mean 'incomparables', presumably with the prefix lost in the handwriting or a slip.

The multiplicity {{{x}},{L∖{x}}} as transcribed does not obviously contain L, so how it links {L} to {{x}} depends on the precise order on M, which is defined on earlier pages. The step is plausible but not verifiable from this page alone.

ideas.what: Connectedness of the poset of multifigures on a finite set L, proved via minimal elements and explicit common upper bounds
ideas.modern_name: Connectedness of a poset/category (zigzag connectivity); in effect, the poset is connected because every element lies above a singleton and the singletons are linked by common upper bounds
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard folklore of order theory and combinatorial topology
ideas.where_published: Possibly analogous connectedness checks in Pursuing Stacks (test categories); not this specific model

ideas.what: Checking an abstract axiom (C4: decomposition into connected components with incomparability across components) in a concrete model of an 'algebra of figures'
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatics of face posets / abstract cell complexes (cf. regular CW complexes, polyhedral complexes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: various (Björner, face-poset theory); the axiom system itself is Grothendieck's unpublished one

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine verification, with degenerate cases, that a concrete poset of multifigures is connected, so one axiom (C4) holds automatically. It is of archival interest only as part of the unpublished 'algèbre des figures' axiomatics. The page has no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Line 'Si card L ≥ 1, alors les X∈M qui sont un élément minimal sont…' should read roughly: 'Si card L ≥ 1 [sic, ≥2], alors les X ∈ M qui ont un élément minimal sont dans la même comp. connexe'. The duplicated garbled line in the transcription is spurious.
'(ce qui suffit pas d'ici à nos yeux)' is probably '(ce qui suffit pour l'instant à nos yeux)'.
'l'axiome C4 [-est ici de-] relatif' is probably 'l'axiome C4 est ici vide/trivial' or similar. The handwriting is unclear, but the sense is that the decomposition is automatic.
'sont comparables' in the parenthesis should be read as 'sont incomparables', which is what the logic requires.
'Le cas des L = comp. connexe' is better read as 'sont dans la même = comp. connexe'.
